objective: Fit per family cost scaling laws from this lab's measured run history, score them by predicting runs held out of the fit, and reprice the three filed naval proposals against the result rather than against the sentence that says no basis exists
rationale: The lab's cost forecasting is measured and bad: zero of three closed pairs land within twenty percent, and sixteen further closed items recorded no actual cost at all, so the binding constraint is the record rather than the forecasting. The strategy asks for per family scaling laws with confidence bands and an auto approval rule at three for three within twenty percent, and that item has never been filed. What makes it fundable now is that the measured history turns out to be much larger than the three scored pairs suggest. A sweep carried out for this filing found measured costs on this box across every family that matters: fifteen free surface cases from 4,800 to 153,600 cells with wall time and rank count recorded per case, seventeen consecutive adjoint gradient evaluations on the same case and design variable set, four periodic hill rungs, four flat plate rungs, thirty six model form cells, and several two arm diagnostics. It also found the structure that a naive fit would miss. Cost is not linear in cells for time accurate free surface work, because halving the wall normal spacing doubles the cells and halves the stability limited timestep; the measured step on that ladder was a factor of eight, not two. Steady mesh ladders scale the other way and have been priced accurately, with two consecutive rungs coming in under estimate. Overrun is concentrated in adjoint, unsteady and multiphase work, and the one eightfold overrun on the record was an estimate built by analogy rather than by measurement. The immediate consequence is a pricing defect currently on the board: one filed naval proposal states in its own basis that no case of its kind has ever been timed here and there is nothing to scale from, and there is
gate: A scored prediction, not a fit. Stage 1: derive the measured corpus mechanically and state its frame, filter and commit; a family enters only with at least four measured points spanning at least a fourfold range in the size variable. Stage 2: for each family, hold out the SINGLE most recent measured run, fit the scaling law on the remainder, and predict the held-out cost with a band, all before looking at the held-out value. Stage 3, the gate: HIT if the held-out actual falls inside the predicted band AND the point prediction is within 20 percent. MISS otherwise. The headline is the hit rate across families, published whatever it is, in the manner the calibration scorecard already publishes zero of three. NO VERDICT for any family with fewer than four points, named rather than dropped. Stage 4: reprice the three filed naval proposals against whichever laws scored HIT, and leave untouched any priced against a family that scored MISS, saying so. IDENTITY TEST, per Verification Charter 2a. Q1, what makes this FAIL: held-out actuals falling outside the predicted bands. Q2, could a wrong treatment still pass? YES, by two routes, and both are closed here. A law fitted on all points including the held-out one reproduces it by construction, which is why the hold-out is declared before the fit and the fit is committed before the actual is read. And a band made wide enough to contain anything passes the containment leg trivially, which is why the 20 percent point criterion is gated alongside it and why the band width itself is reported per family. EXTERNAL REFERENT, per Verification Charter 6a: NONE, and this is stated rather than glossed. These are this lab's own measured costs on this lab's own box, and no published value exists for what a solve should cost here. The held-out actual is external to the FIT, which is the only independence this design can claim, and it is claimed as exactly that and no more.
cost_basis: Zero solver compute. Every input is a cost already paid and already written down; the work is extraction, fitting and scoring. Basis gross, on the charter's binding unit of wall seconds times ranks divided by sixty, which every figure in the corpus already uses. The extraction is bounded and its cheapest part is already done: the sweep behind this filing located the per evaluation ledgers, the per rung cost tables and the per cell records, and confirmed that the durable archive holds 477 run directories while the central registry records a cost figure for only 3 of its 142 completion records. That asymmetry is the reason this is a fitting task rather than a query, and it is also the second deliverable: the families with no recoverable cost are named, which is the list the record needs before the next sixteen items close without one
expected_knowledge_gain: The lab either gains a defensible way to price work or learns that it cannot price its own work, and both are worth having before several thousand core minutes of naval proposals are bought. The strategy makes forecasts auto approve at three for three within twenty percent; today the score is zero of three, so nothing auto approves and every estimate is argued rather than derived. A per family hit rate replaces that argument with a number, and it is the number that decides whether the auto approval rule is reachable at all. There is a sharper near term gain: three filed naval proposals carry estimates of 135, 900 and 3,000 core minutes, and at least one is priced against a stated absence of measured history that a sweep contradicts. Repricing them before purchase is the cheapest correction available to the largest planned spend on the board. The finding that a time accurate free surface refinement step cost a factor of eight rather than the factor of four a cell count argument predicts is the single most load bearing input to any wave or hull estimate, and it is currently written in one results record and used in no proposal
hard_criterion_note: Starts no flow case. It reads costs already paid and predicts nothing that requires a new one
